insights.claim_template: {measure:depreciated_share} of gross PP&E is already depreciated; the remaining net book value of {money:net_book_value} carries {measure:remaining_book_life} of life at the current annual charge of {money:annual_da}.
insights.formula: Accumulated depreciation ÷ gross PP&E; net book value ÷ annual D&A = remaining book life

measures.label: Remaining book life at current charge

narrative.explanation: 70.4% of gross PP&E is already depreciated; the remaining net book value of RON 11,728,539.67 carries 4.0 years of life at the current annual charge of RON 2,955,346.39. Graded high: the amount at stake is 70.4% of gross pp&e, against the ladder printed beside this finding. Depreciation is graded against the asset base that produced it, so a factory and a courier are compared on the share of their OWN gross PP&E already written off rather than on an absolute charge.
narrative.reason: the advisory lane was not invoked for this build
narrative.so_what: Ask for the fixed-asset register by acquisition year and the committed capex plan. A book this far through its depreciation life either has replacement spending ahead of it or is running assets past their useful life, and the two have very different cash consequences.

insights.rank_basis: Ranked by severity level, then by materiality descending; ties broken by detector id ascending. The top 5 carry into the executive summary.

severity.why: Depreciation is graded against the asset base that produced it, so a factory and a courier are compared on the share of their OWN gross PP&E already written off rather than on an absolute charge.

insights.claim_template: {money:related_party} of related-party and other-debtor receivables is {measure:share_of_assets} of total assets and {measure:share_of_equity} of equity; written off in full, the equity ratio moves from {measure:equity_ratio} to {measure:equity_ratio_haircut} and the current ratio from {measure:current_ratio} to {measure:current_ratio_haircut}.

insights.claim_template: Rebuilding the P&L from the movement columns reaches {money:reconstructed}; statutory profit in account 121 is {money:statutory}. The unexplained step of {money:step} is {measure:graded_share} of the {money:graded_base} it is bridging.

Graded medium: the amount at stake is 16.6% of reconstructed net income, against the ladder printed beside this finding. The step is graded against the profit it is correcting. insights.claim_template: The net trade float is {money:float}: {money:trade_receivables} owed by customers against {money:trade_payables} owed to suppliers — {measure:dso} of sales outstanding against {measure:dpo} of payables, a gap of {measure:float_days}.
insights.formula: DSO = trade receivables net ÷ revenue × 365; DPO = trade payables ÷ cost of goods sold × 365; float = trade receivables net − trade payables

narrative.explanation: The net trade float is RON 1,327,011.19: RON 8,513,384.96 owed by customers against RON 7,186,373.77 owed to suppliers — 28.0 days of sales outstanding against 37.2 days of payables, a gap of -9.1 days. Graded low: the amount at stake is 1.2% of revenue, against the ladder printed beside this finding. Trade float is a claim on a year of trading, so it is graded as a share of that year's revenue — the same base both day counts already annualise against.
narrative.reason: the advisory lane was not invoked for this build
narrative.so_what: Compare the collection gap with the credit terms actually granted. Where suppliers fund the cycle, that funding is a payables line that can be withdrawn, not a permanent source.
